channel.title: Creator Toolkit Blog
channel.description: Practical YouTube guides for creators, one for each free tool.

item.title: Do YouTube Tags Matter? How to See a Video's Tags and What to Do With Them
item.description: What YouTube says about tags, how to see the tags a public video exposes, why copying another creator's tags is not a ranking shortcut, and what to focus on instead.

item.title: How to Make a YouTube Subscribe Link (and Why It Cannot Force a Subscribe)
item.description: How the sub_confirmation=1 parameter works on a channel link, where it helps, where it does not appear, and why you can never subscribe someone automatically.

item.title: How to Check the Public Stats of Any YouTube Video (and What They Hide)
item.description: See a video's public views, likes, upload date and duration, understand the like-to-view rate, and learn why view counts can lag, freeze or differ from what the owner sees in Studio.

item.title: How to Make a YouTube Link That Opens the App From Your Bio
item.description: Why YouTube links in Instagram, TikTok and Facebook bios often open in a browser, how an app link page tries to help, and what no tool can force.

item.title: How to Use Creative Commons and Free Footage in YouTube Videos Without Trouble
item.description: What a Creative Commons license on YouTube actually allows, how to credit the author properly, where to look for free clips, and where fair use does and does not help.

item.title: What Is the Best Time to Post on YouTube? Find Yours in Five Minutes
item.description: There is no universal best time to post on YouTube. Here is how to find when your own viewers are online and how to convert that into a publish time in your own time zone.

item.title: How to Add Chapters to a YouTube Video (Rules, Format and Common Errors)
item.description: The exact rules YouTube sets for video chapters - first timestamp at 0:00, at least three, 10 seconds minimum - with a format example and the common reasons chapters do not show.

item.title: How Much Do YouTube Creators Earn? RPM and CPM Explained
item.description: What RPM and CPM mean, why your real RPM is lower than a CPM you read about, and how to use a revenue estimator as a scenario tool rather than a prediction.

item.title: How to Compare Two YouTube Thumbnails Before You Publish
item.description: Preview thumbnail and title pairs in a mock YouTube feed in dark and light mode, and learn how YouTube's own Test and Compare feature measures real viewers.

item.title: A YouTube Title and Description Checklist (With the Limits That Matter)
item.description: What to check before you publish - title length, keyword placement, the first lines of the description, hashtags, chapters and links - and what a checklist score can and cannot tell you.

item.title: YouTube Keyword Research With Autocomplete (and How to Pick Hashtags)
item.description: How to find real search phrases using YouTube's search suggestions, what they do and do not tell you, and how to choose hashtags without breaking YouTube's rules.

item.title: YouTube Channel Stats Lookup - What Public Data Can and Cannot Tell You
item.description: What you can learn about any YouTube channel from public data - subscribers, recent uploads, views and likes - and what you can only see with channel owner access.

item.title: How to Clean and Convert SRT and VTT Caption Files
item.description: Remove style tags and sound cues, merge repeated lines, shift timing and convert between SRT, VTT and plain text, all in your browser without uploading the file.

item.title: How to Get a YouTube Transcript (and Download It as TXT, SRT or VTT)
item.description: Three ways to read or download a YouTube video's transcript, what auto-generated captions get wrong, and when a video has no transcript at all.

item.title: A YouTube Channel Audit Checklist You Can Finish in 30 Minutes
item.description: A practical 20-point YouTube channel audit covering setup, content, discoverability and consistency, with the reason behind each check and what to ignore.

item.title: YouTube Partner Program Requirements Explained (500 vs 1,000 Subscribers)
item.description: The two YouTube Partner Program tiers in plain English - 500 subscribers for fan funding, 1,000 for ad revenue - with the exact watch hour and Shorts view numbers from YouTube's help pages.

item.title: YouTube Title Ideas That Work Without Clickbait
item.description: How to turn a topic into clear YouTube titles and tags, with ten proven title angles and the limits of any title generator.

item.title: How to Download a YouTube Thumbnail in Every Size
item.description: Get the thumbnail image of any public YouTube video in every available size, plus the official size and format rules for your own thumbnails.
